        "originType": "home",
        "sampleTypeId": amber_id,
        "containerType": "ambient_insulated_box",
        "temperatureMinC": 15.0,
        "temperatureMaxC": 25.0,
        "requestedAt": "2026-09-17T21:00:00Z",
        "deliveryDeadline": "2026-09-17T23:00:00Z",
        "earliestCollectionAt": "2026-09-17T21:10:00Z",
        "latestCollectionAt": "2026-09-17T21:40:00Z",
        "idempotencyKey": f"test_req_{int(time.time())}"
    }
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/create-collection-request", json=req_payload, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code in [200, 201], f"Create collection request failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    created_sample = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    sample_id = created_sample.get("id") or created_sample.get("sampleId")
    assert sample_id, f"Sample ID missing in creation response: {created_sample}"
    print("✓ Created collection request successfully. Sample ID:", sample_id)

    # 8. List role work as collection_professional
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/select-active-role", json={"role": "collection_professional"}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Select role collection_professional failed: {r.status_code}"
    print("✓ Switched role to collection_professional")

    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/list-role-work", json={"role": "collection_professional"}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"List role work failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    work_list = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    print(f"✓ Collection professional work list retrieved ({len(work_list)} items)")

    assignment = next((w for w in work_list if (w.get("sampleId") == sample_id or w.get("sample_id") == sample_id)), None)
    if assignment:
        assignment_id = assignment.get("id") or assignment.get("assignmentId")
        print("✓ Found assignment for sample:", assignment_id)

        # Accept assignment
        r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/accept-assignment", json={"assignmentId": assignment_id, "idempotencyKey": f"acc_{int(time.time())}"}, headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Accept assignment failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        print("✓ Accepted collection assignment")

        # Record worker location
        r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/record-worker-location", json={
            "assignmentId": assignment_id,
            "coordinate": {"latitude": 12.9750, "longitude": 77.6000},
            "sequence": 1,
            "recordedAt": "2026-09-17T21:15:00Z"
        }, headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Record worker location failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        print("✓ Recorded worker location")

        # Collect and seal sample
        r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/collect-and-seal-sample", json={
            "sampleId": sample_id,
            "assignmentId": assignment_id,
            "collectedAt": "2026-09-17T21:20:00Z",
            "containerType": "ambient_insulated_box",
            "observedTemperatureC": 20.5,
            "idempotencyKey": f"col_{int(time.time())}"
        }, headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Collect & seal failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        print("✓ Sample collected and sealed")

        # Record handling checkpoint
        r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/record-handling-checkpoint", json={
            "sampleId": sample_id,
            "assignmentId": assignment_id,
            "containerType": "ambient_insulated_box",
            "observedTemperatureC": 21.0,
            "recordedAt": "2026-09-17T21:22:00Z",
            "idempotencyKey": f"chk_{int(time.time())}"
        }, headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Checkpoint failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        print("✓ Handling checkpoint recorded")

    # 9. Test Ingest Presealed Sample
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/select-active-role", json={"role": "node_handler"}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    presealed_payload = {
        "origin": {"latitude": 12.9784, "longitude": 77.6408},
        "originType": "collection_center",
        "originNodeId": "a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",
        "sampleTypeId": amber_id,
        "containerType": "ambient_insulated_box",
        "temperatureMinC": 15.0,
        "temperatureMaxC": 25.0,
        "requestedAt": "2026-09-17T21:00:00Z",
        "deliveryDeadline": "2026-09-17T23:30:00Z",
        "idempotencyKey": f"presealed_{int(time.time())}"
    }
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/ingest-presealed-sample", json=presealed_payload, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code in [200, 201], f"Ingest presealed sample failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    presealed_sample = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    presealed_id = presealed_sample.get("id") or presealed_sample.get("sampleId")
    print("✓ Ingested pre-sealed sample successfully. Sample ID:", presealed_id)

    # 10. Switch to Dispatcher and test operations
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/select-active-role", json={"role": "dispatcher"}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/read-operations-state", json={}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Read operations state failed: {r.status_code}"
    ops_state = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    print(f"✓ Dispatcher operations state: {len(ops_state.get('samples', []))} samples, {len(ops_state.get('workers', []))} workers")

    # Read sample lifecycle
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/read-sample-lifecycle", json={"sampleId": sample_id}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Read sample lifecycle failed: {r.status_code}"
    lifecycle = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    print(f"✓ Sample lifecycle retrieved with {len(lifecycle.get('events', []))} timeline events")

    # Search audit trail
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/search-audit-trail", json={"entityId": sample_id}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Search audit trail failed: {r.status_code}"
    audit_res = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    print(f"✓ Audit trail searched: {len(audit_res.get('entries', []))} records found")

    # 11. Admin Management
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/select-active-role", json={"role": "administrator"}, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200

    # Create location
    new_loc_payload = {
        "name": "Electronic City Hub",
        "coordinate": {"latitude": 12.8399, "longitude": 77.6770},
        "coverageKm": 5.0,
        "handlingMinutes": 10,
        "active": True,
        "functions": {
            "collectionPoint": True,
            "transferPoint": True,
            "hub": True,
            "laboratory": False
        }
    }
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/create-location", json=new_loc_payload, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code in [200, 201], f"Create location failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    new_loc = r.json().get("data", r.json())
    new_loc_id = new_loc.get("id") or new_loc.get("locationId")
    print("✓ Created new location:", new_loc_id)

    # Configure capacity
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/configure-capacity", json={
        "resourceId": new_loc_id,
        "capacityUnits": 150,
        "cooledCapacityUnits": 75
    }, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Configure capacity failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    print("✓ Configured location capacity")

    # Create connection
    r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/create-connection", json={
        "fromLocationId": "a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
        "toLocationId": new_loc_id,
        "travelMinutes": 30,
        "costUnits": 20.0,
        "cooled": True,
        "active": True
    }, headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code in [200, 201], f"Create connection failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
    print("✓ Created connection")

    print("=== ALL INTEGRATION TESTS PASSED SUCCESSFULLY ===")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_tests()

USER_CONTEXT: Build and verify the full-stack "lab-sample-pickup-and-delivery" application strictly complying with `INSTRUCTION.md`, `contracts/openapi.contract.json`, and `contracts/ui.contract.json`. Serve offline map assets at `/opt/arena/map-assets/` (PMTiles, fonts, sprites, style.json) without external network calls.

TASK_TRACKING:
- TASK-001: Inspect workspace, dependencies, and environment [COMPLETED]
- TASK-002: Backend API handlers, models, routing engine, offline maps, and DB services [COMPLETED]
- TASK-003: Frontend React dashboard with MapLibre offline maps and role views [COMPLETED]
- TASK-004: Create and verify setup scripts in `app-setup/` (`build.sh`, `start.sh`, `reset.sh`) [COMPLETED]
- TASK-005: Verify service lifecycle (`start.sh`, `reset.sh`), database migrations, seed data, and initial admin [IN_PROGRESS]
- TASK-006: End-to-end contract validation and functional UI/API testing [PENDING]

COMPLETED:
- Updated `/workspace/frontend/src/api.ts` to match backend payload contracts.
- Created executable setup scripts (`/workspace/app-setup/build.sh`, `start.sh`, `reset.sh`).
- Successfully executed `/workspace/app-setup/build.sh`, compiling both the Go binary and React frontend assets into `dist/`.

PENDING:
- Test running `reset.sh` to initialize/seed the PostgreSQL database.
- Start server via `start.sh` and verify `/ready`, `/api`, and frontend serving at port 8080.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is an image file (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .bmp), `view` displays the image content
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.

  working directory changes persist across commands.

  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.

  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.

* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if not given, no string will be added). Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If none is given, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

function.name: finish
function.description:
Signals the completion of the current task or conversation.

Use this tool when:
- You have successfully completed the user's requested task
- You cannot proceed further due to technical limitations or missing information

The message should include:
- A clear summary of actions taken and their results
- Any next steps for the user
- Explanation if you're unable to complete the task
- Any follow-up questions if more information is needed

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

message.description: Final message to send to the user.

function.name: think
function.description:
Use the tool to think about something. It will not obtain new information or make any changes to the repository, but just log the thought. Use it when complex reasoning or brainstorming is needed.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.
2. After receiving test results, use this tool to brainstorm ways to fix failing tests.
3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.
